record.context_brief: Largest code in a finite metric space
record.original_question: Given a finite metric space X^n with metric D, and fixed integers n and d, determine the largest integer M for which there exists a code C contained in X^n having minimum distance d and cardinality M.

evidence.quote: Open Question 3.3. Given a finite metric space Xn and a metric D, fix n and d. Find the largest M such that there exists a code C ⊆ Xn, with minimum distance d, and M = |C|.

artifact.category_tag: bounds on codes in metric spaces
artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $(X^n, D)$ be a finite metric space, where $X^n$ denotes a set equipped with a metric $D : X^n \times X^n \to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$. A code is any subset $C \subseteq X^n$, and the minimum distance of $C$ is defined as $\min\{D(x,y) : x,y \in C,\ x \neq y\}$. Fix positive integers $n$ and $d$. Determine the largest integer $M = M(X^n, D, d)$ such that there exists a code $C \subseteq X^n$ with minimum distance at least $d$ and $|C| = M$.
artifact.status_search_result: This is the general form of the fundamental coding-theory problem of determining $A(n,d)$ (and its analogues in arbitrary finite metric spaces). It remains open in general; exact values of $A(n,d)$ for the Hamming metric are unknown for most parameter ranges, and only bounds (Singleton, Hamming, Plotkin, Elias–Bassalygo, linear programming, etc.) are known. No general closed-form solution exists.

status_evidence.title: Bounds on codes - Wikipedia/standard reference
status_evidence.snippet: Determining A(n,d), the maximum size of a code of length n and minimum distance d, is a central open problem in coding theory; only bounds are known in general.
status_evidence.claim: The general problem of determining the maximum size of a code with given length and minimum distance is open.
